candidates.attacker_control: An authenticated Karaf console/SSH (or equivalent) user supplies the `--java-opts/-o` string to `instance:start`, `instance:restart`, or `instance:create` (stored in instance.properties and later reused by start/restart), and can also choose the instance name used in the root-instance restart command. These values are passed verbatim into the concatenated command line.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: javaOpts is documented as JVM options, but no validation/escaping is applied and the value is not confined to a Java argument (shell parses the whole line). Checked the default command ACLs: assemblies/features/standard/src/main/feature/feature.xml restricts `shell` scope `exec/new/nano/java` to admin and defines ACLs for config/feature scopes, but contains no `org.apache.karaf.command.acl.instance` entry, and SecuredSessionFactoryImpl.checkSecurity() allows the call when no ACL/compulsory roles apply. Checked that the `instance` feature is included in the default assembly (assemblies/apache-karaf/pom.xml around line 173). Checked ProcessBuilderImpl/ProcessImpl: the jpm layer does not quote `${command}` (only double-quote escaping on Windows in ProcessImpl.create), so the injection reaches /bin/sh. Did not execute anything; runtime confirmation is not claimed.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary OS command execution as the user running the Karaf server, reachable from a merely authenticated console user and bypassing the default `shell:exec = admin` command ACL; can lead to full host/service compromise and persistence. The restart path also allows injecting through the instance name and javaOpts.
candidates.prerequisites: Authenticated console/SSH access (the `instance` command scope has no default command-ACL entry in the standard distribution, while `shell:exec` is admin-restricted, so a non-admin role suffices); the `instance` feature is present in the default distribution's boot features; the attacker must be able to create/start an instance (default `karaf.instances` location is writable by the Karaf process). On Unix the jpm start.sh path is used; Windows uses cscript/vbs with the same raw substitution pattern.
candidates.root_cause: InstanceServiceImpl builds the child JVM invocation as one raw string, concatenating user-controlled values: javaOpts/opts (from instance:create -o / instance:start -o / instance:restart -o), the instance name (restart path), and location-derived canonical paths. The string is handed to org.apache.karaf.jpm ProcessBuilder.command(...) -> ProcessImpl.create(...) -> ScriptUtils.execute("start", props), which writes util/src/main/resources/org/apache/karaf/jpm/impl/unix/start.sh and executes it with /bin/sh. That script contains `nohup ${command} &` with no quoting/escaping, so shell metacharacters embedded in the option value are interpreted by /bin/sh and execute arbitrary commands in the Karaf server account. The same unquoted-substitution pattern exists in the Windows .vbs template path.
candidates.title: OS command injection through instance --java-opts/name into the unquoted jpm start script
candidates.trace: StartCommand.doExecute() takes javaOpts -> Instance.start(opts) -> InstanceServiceImpl.startInstance()/restartInstance() -> doStart() builds `"<java>" <opts> <karafOpts> <jdkOpts> ... -classpath ... org.apache.karaf.main.Main server` -> ProcessBuilderFactoryImpl.newBuilder().command(command).start() -> ProcessImpl.create(dir, command) puts the string in `${command}` -> ScriptUtils.execute("start", props) writes the template and runs `/bin/sh start.sh` -> start.sh line 28 `nohup ${command} &` performs word splitting/expansion on the unquoted value, allowing `;`, `&&`, backticks, `$(...)`, `#`, redirections, etc.
candidates.unverified: Whether all supported configurations let a non-admin user run instance commands (depends on user roles/any custom ACLs), and whether the benchmark's ground-truth issue is this path rather than another candidate lead. The exact shell parsing of a crafted option value was not executed; it follows from start.sh's unquoted `${command}`.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-78 OS Command Injection (argument/option value not escaped before shell execution)

coverage_summary: Read the scope report (1,851 files, no sensitive/symlink/binary exclusions beyond the stated NUL-byte policy). Surveyed build/config and inspected the main security-relevant runtime modules: instance (commands, services, jpm/ScriptUtils), shell core + secured session/ACL + ssh, management (JMX guard, authenticators), config (commands, repository, MBean), kar (extraction/name handling), features (model parsing, config installer, deployers), wrapper, obr, profile, jaas (properties/JDBC/LDAP/publickey), util (XmlUtils, JaasHelper, jpm), webconsole plugins, and selected build-tooling code. Grepped for command-execution, file-write, XML-parser, deserialization, TLS, and traversal patterns; traced the strongest input-to-sink chain across files. Not exhaustively line-reviewed: large subsystems such as features Deployer/FeaturesServiceImpl, profile Builder/assembly, most tooling Maven plugins, specs bundles, and the webconsole Terminal/gogo internals.
limitations: No code execution, tests, or scanners were run; findings are source-evidence only and runtime exploitability is not confirmed.
No git history/patch information was available, so the specific upstream fix/CVE associated with this snapshot could not be identified; the one-candidate choice is based on source evidence strength.
Large files (e.g. features Deployer 80KB, profile Builder 100KB, webconsole Terminal 58KB, tooling MoJos) were only selectively read, so an additional issue there cannot be excluded.
The rejected leads were not exhaustively validated (e.g., Felix ConfigAdmin PID acceptance and FileInstall/JAAS reload semantics were not verified).

rejected_leads.lead: Config PID / factory alias / --type suffix path traversal: ConfigRepositoryImpl.generateConfigFilename() and createFactoryConfiguration() build `new File(karaf.etc, pid + "." + suffix)` / `factoryPid + "-" + alias + "." + suffix` with no traversal validation, unlike config:install/MBean which check `finalname.contains("..")`. Could allow arbitrary file write (e.g. overwriting etc/users.properties for manager->admin).
rejected_leads.reason: Real weakness but weaker evidence chain: it depends on Felix ConfigAdmin accepting the crafted PID/factory alias and on file/timing behavior of FileInstall/JAAS reload; impact is file write rather than direct command execution. Left as an unconfirmed lead, not the submitted candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Kar.getKarName() returns the Maven artifact segment of a `mvn:` URI without validation, and KarServiceImpl.install() uses it in `new File(storage, karName)` for extraction and error-path recursive deletion.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires admin-level kar:install invocation and an unusual mvn URI; the KAR entry extraction itself already rejects '..' entries. Lower impact relative to the instance injection.

rejected_leads.lead: wrapper:install --name is used unvalidated in file paths (etc/<name>-wrapper.conf, bin/<name>-service, systemd/<name>.service).
rejected_leads.reason: Arbitrary-write shape but content is template-driven and the command is normally privileged; no clear privilege boundary crossed.

rejected_leads.lead: obr FileUtil.unjar() uses a canonical-path startsWith() prefix check that can be bypassed for sibling paths sharing a prefix.
rejected_leads.reason: Vendored OBR utility, requires OBR command use; no strong cross-boundary trace found in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: JMX KarafMBeanServerGuard only guards invoke/get/set attributes; other MBeanServerConnection operations (createMBean, registerMBean, MLet creation) are not RBAC-checked.
rejected_leads.reason: MLet addUrl/getMBeansFromURL are explicitly blocked; no concrete RCE path demonstrated from the guard-only coverage, so it remains speculative.

rejected_leads.lead: XML parsing surfaces (features, KAR, deployer, Maven config, log config).
rejected_leads.reason: Most parsers set secure-processing/disallow-doctype/external-entity flags; no missing-hardening path with an untrusted input was confirmed.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Karaf 4.3.5 source snapshot (1,851 readable files; binaries/symlinks excluded by the scope filters). The strongest source-evidenced issue is an OS command injection in the instance-management path: user-supplied Java options (and, on the root-instance restart path, the instance name) are concatenated into a single command string that the jpm layer renders unquoted as `${command}` inside a `/bin/sh` script (`nohup ${command} &`). The default distribution boots the `instance` feature, and there is no default command ACL for the `instance` scope, whereas `shell:exec` is restricted to `admin` — so a lower-privileged authenticated console user can reach host command execution. Other leads (config PID/alias path traversal, KAR name traversal, wrapper:install `--name`, OBR prefix check, JMX guard coverage, XML parsers) were examined but are weaker or already mitigated, and are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
